questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Queen Elizabeth I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **East India Company** was granted a charter by **Queen Elizabeth I** in **1600.**
 
• This charter gave the company a monopoly on **English trade with the East Indies**, which included modern-day** India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Indonesia.**
 
• The East India Company played a significant role in **British colonialism and imperialism, **establishing trade relationships and political control over large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Queen Elizabeth I's charter for the East India Company was a key moment in the history of **British imperialism and global trade**, paving the way for centuries of British economic and political influence in Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Edward VI **(reigned 1547-1553) was the **son of Henry VIII **and ruled England for a brief period before his death at the age of 15.
 
• **King Henry IV **(reigned 1399-1413) was the** first monarch **of the House of Lancaster and played a key role in the** English civil war **known as the **Wars of the Roses.**
 
• **Queen Victoria** (reigned 1837-1901) oversaw the height of the **British Empire's global power and influence**, but her reign came long after the **East India Company **had been dissolved and replaced by the British Raj in India.
 
• The **East India Company **was a joint-stock company that was founded in** 1600 and dissolved in 1874,** after centuries of trade and political control in India and other parts of Asia.

questions.question: Among the following, which of these are an example of capital receipt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Borrowings and loan recovery.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital receipt** refers to the** inflow of funds** that do not result from the** regular business operations** of a company.
 
• **Borrowings** and** loan recovery** are examples of **capital receipts** because they involve the** inflow of funds** that are not generated from the company's regular business activities.
 
• **Borrowings** refer to the funds borrowed by a company from **external sources** such as **banks or financial institutions.**
 
• **Loan recovery **refers to the **repayment of loans** that were previously taken by the company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rent and commission received, sale of goods and rent, and commission and dividend received are not examples of capital receipt because they are generated from the** regular business operations** of a company.
 
• **Rent and commission** received are** revenues earned by a company** for providing services or renting out property.
 
• **Sale of goods** and rent refers to the sale of goods and the** rental income earned from that sale.**
 
• **Commission and dividend** received are payments made to a company for services rendered or as a **return on investment in shares.**

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which among the following has the minimum population density?

• **Andhra Pradesh** has a population density of **308 persons per square kilometer **and **Sikkim **has a population density of **86 persons per square kilometer.**
 
• **Population density** is the number of **people living** in a particular **area per unit of land.**
 
• It is an important indicator of the **level of development and resource use **in a region.

• It is one of the** most planned cities** in India and has a high standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** is a state in southern India with a population of over **49 million.**
 
 
• It is the **seventh-largest state** in India by area and the** tenth-largest by population.**
 
 
 
• **Sikkim** is a state in **northeastern India **and is the least populous state in the country.
 
 
• It is known for its natural beauty and is a **popular tourist destination.**

questions.question: Article 356 and 360 in the Indian constitution are the articles based on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**emergency provisions.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 356** is related to the** imposition of President's Rule** in a state, which is a form of** emergency provision** used when the state government is unable to function properly.
 
• **Article 360** deals with the** financial emergency** that can be imposed in the country when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.
 
• The emergency provisions in the Indian constitution are of three types -** national emergency, state emergency, and financial emergency.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional languages** are not directly related to either Article 356 or 360, although language can be a factor in the** imposition of President's Rule** in a state.
 
• **Amendment of the constitution** is not related to these articles, as it is covered under a separate set of articles in the constitution.

questions.question: How many white squares are there on a chessboard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 32.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **standard chessboard **has** 64 squares **in total, with **32** of them being **white** and the other **32 being black.**
 
• Since each white square is adjacent to a **black square,** the number of** white squares **and **black squares** is the same.
 
• Therefore, the number of white squares on a chessboard is** 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chess is a** two-player strategy game** that is played on a square board with 64 squares arranged in an** 8x8 grid.**
 
• Each player starts with **16 pieces,** including **one king, one queen, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, and eight pawns.**
 
• The game is won by putting the opponent's king in **"checkmate,"** a position in which the king is in a threatened position and cannot escape capture on the next move.

questions.question: Which vitamin is soluble in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin - C.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin C** is a **water-soluble vitamin,** which means it **dissolves in water** and is excreted through urine if there is an excess intake. 
 
• Water-soluble vitamins are **not stored in the body **to a great extent and need to be replenished through** regular intake of foods** rich in these vitamins.
 
• **Vitamin D** is a **fat-soluble vitamin,** which means it **dissolves in fat **and is stored in the body's** fatty tissues and liver.**
 
• **Vitamin E** is also a** fat-soluble vitamin** that helps** protect cells from damage** caused by **free radicals.**
 
• **Vitamin A** is another** fat-soluble vitamin **that is important for **vision, immune function, and skin health.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin D** is important for **bone health** as it helps the body absorb** calcium and phosphorus** from the diet.
 
• **Vitamin E **is found in **nuts, seeds, and vegetable oils **and plays a role in protecting **cell membranes from damage**.
 
• **Vitamin A** is found in animal products like** liver, eggs, and milk,** as well as in some plant-based foods like **sweet potatoes and carrots**.
 
• Excess intake of fat-soluble vitamins can lead to** toxicity,** as they are stored in the body for longer periods and are** not excreted** as easily as water-soluble vitamins.

questions.question: The breaking up of the rocks on the earth's surface is called as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** weathering.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weathering** is the process of** breaking down rocks, soils, and minerals** through exposure to the earth's **atmosphere, water, and biological organisms.**
 
• There are two types of weathering:** mechanical and chemical.**
 
• Mechanical weathering involves the **physical breakdown** of rocks into smaller pieces, while chemical weathering involves the **chemical alteration** of rocks through reactions with water, air, and other substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stacking** refers to the process of **piling up rocks or other materials**, typically for** construction or landscaping purposes.**
 
• **Meandering** refers to the winding or curving of a **river or stream**, typically due to changes in the landscape or the flow of water.
 
• **Sorting** can refer to several processes, including the **separation of materials **based on **size or weight,** or the categorization of objects based on certain criteria.

questions.question: The Himalayan Mountain range was formed by the collision of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Plate and Eurasian Plate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Himalayan Mountain range** was formed by the collision of the **Eurasian Plate and the Indian Plate.**
 
• This collision began around **50 million years ago** and is still ongoing, causing the Himalayas to rise at a rate of about **5 mm per year.**
 
• The collision of the two plates caused the Indian Plate to be pushed underneath the** Eurasian Plate,** creating immense pressure and heat that led to the formation of the** Himalayan Mountains. **
 
• The Himalayas are the **highest and youngest mountain range** in the world and are home to some of the **tallest peaks**, including Mount Everest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **African Plate** and** Australian Plate** are both located far away from the **Indian Plate and Eurasian Plate**, making it impossible for them to have contributed to the formation of the Himalayas.
 
• The collision between the** Indian Plate and African Plate **did occur, but it happened much earlier, around **200 million years ago**, and led to the formation of the **supercontinent Gondwana.**
 
• **The Eurasian Plate** is the largest tectonic plate on Earth, covering most of **Europe and Asia**.
 
 
• It is also responsible for the formation of other mountain ranges, such as the **Alps and the Ural Mountains.**

questions.question: The basic unit of speed of an object is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**metre per second (m/s).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The basic unit of speed of an object is **metre per second (m/s).**
 
• The speed of an object is defined as the rate at which it** covers a distance** in a given time.
 
• It is used to **express the speed of objects** that move relatively faster than the speed of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metre per km** (m/km) is** not** a standard unit of speed.
 
• **Metre per hour** (m/h) is a unit of speed but it is not the basic unit of speed.
 
 
• It is used to express the speed of objects that move **relatively slower than the speed of light.**
 
 
 
• **Metre per minute** (m/m) is also not the basic unit of speed.
 
 
• It is used to express the speed of objects that move **relatively slower than the speed of light.**

The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kicheri **is a **harvest festival **celebrated majorly in **Uttar Pradesh, India.**
 
• This festival is also known as **Kheer-Chawal Mela**, and it is celebrated during the month of **Kartik (October-November)** as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• The festival involves** ritual bathing** in the holy rivers like **Ganga, Yamuna, and Sarayu.**
 
• People prepare and distribute **Kheer** (a sweet dish made of rice and milk) as **Prasad **among the **devotees and the poor.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In** Madhya Pradesh,** the **harvest festival** is known as **Hareli**, which is celebrated during the month of **Shravana (July-August).**
 
• In **Haryana**, the harvest festival is called **Jitiya,** which is observed during the month of **Bhadrapada (August-September).**
 
• In **Gujarat**, the harvest festival is known as **Navratri, **which is celebrated for nine days during the month of **Ashwin (September-October).**

questions.question: In which of the following methods of irrigation, the water falls drop by drop directly near the roots?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drip system.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The method of irrigation where** water falls drop by drop** directly near the roots is called the** drip system.**
 
• This method is also known as** micro-irrigation** as it uses small amounts of water over a **longer period of time. **
 
• The drip system is** highly efficient **as it **reduces water loss** due to evaporation and runoff.
 
• This method is particularly useful in areas where water is **scarce or expensive.**
 
• Manual irrigation involves **watering plants by hand**, whereas sprinkler systems and lateral move irrigation involve **spraying water** over a larger area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sprinkler systems** involve **spraying water **over a large area, similar to rain.

 
 
• They are commonly used in **agriculture and landscaping.**
 
 
 
• **Lateral move irrigation** is a type of **mechanized irrigation** where a large sprinkler is moved along a linear path to **cover a rectangular area.**
 
• **Drip irrigation** is also used in home **gardens and greenhouses** to provide precise amounts of **water to each plant**.
 
• The key word **"irrigation"** refers to the **artificial application of water** to plants to help them grow.

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated in the Battle of Kannauj in 1540?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Kannauj** was fought between the **Mughal Emperor Humayun** and the **Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri** in **1540.**
 
• Sher Shah Suri emerged **victorious in the battle** and** Humayun** was forced to** flee to Iran**.
 
• The battle is considered as a turning point in the history of India as it marked the** end of the Mughal rule **and the beginning of the **Sur dynasty.**
 
• Sher Shah Suri went on to establish a** strong administration** and introduced various reforms, such as the introduction of the **rupee as a currency** and the construction of the **Grand Trunk Road.**
 
• **Akbar,** who was the son of **Humayun,** later **defeated the Sur dynasty **and established the **Mughal rule **in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hemu,** also known as Hemchandra Vikramaditya, was a** Hindu king** who ruled over **Delhi **in the **16th century.**
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** was a **Pashtun warrior **who rose to power after defeating the **Mughal Emperor Humayun.**
 
 
• He is known for his **administrative and military reforms **and is considered as one of the greatest rulers of **medieval India. **
 
 
 
• **Akbar** was the **third Mughal Emperor **who ruled over India from **1556 to 1605.**
 
 
• He is known for his** religious tolerance, military conquests, and cultural achievements.**
 
 
 
• **Humayun **was the **second Mughal Emperor** who ruled over India from **1530 to 1540 **and from** 1555 to 1556.**
 
 
• He was known for his** military failures** and was forced to flee to Iran after his defeat in the Battle of Kannauj.
